No Permit for Private-Property Tree Removal

Auburn Township and Geauga County do not require a permit to remove a tree on private residential property. That keeps most Auburn Township removals simpler than in the estate villages to the west — no village filing, no plan-of-work submission, and no waiting on review before the crew can work.

Large-scale clearing can trigger a zoning review, and any right-of-way or tree-lawn work is coordinated with the township separately. Roubic confirms the requirement for your specific address as part of the free on-site estimate, so there are no surprises.

EAB Ash Stability Degradation

Emerald Ash Borer has killed an estimated 90%+ of NE Ohio's ash. Standing dead ash in Auburn Township turns brittle within 18–24 months and fails violently in storms — the fragile ones are already dead.

Ice & Wind-Load Failures

Auburn Township's mature rural canopy takes hard ice and wind hits every winter and spring. A leaning or dead-crown tree near a house or driveway becomes an insurance-deductible emergency overnight.

Emergency Premium

A planned removal is a scheduled job. The same tree after it falls is an after-hours emergency at a 30% premium — plus any cleanup, structure repair, and access-clearing the failure creates.

Common Auburn Township Removal Questions

Auburn Township Tree Removal FAQ

Six things Auburn Township homeowners want to know before booking.

How much does tree removal cost in Auburn Township?
Tree removal in Auburn Township typically runs $300–$7,000+ depending on size, species, access, and equipment. Confirmed brackets: small under 30 ft $300–$700; medium 30–60 ft $700–$1,800; large 60–80 ft heritage oak $1,800–$3,500; X-large or crane-assisted 80+ ft $3,500–$7,000+. After-hours emergency work carries a 30% premium. Every on-site estimate is free.
Do I need a permit to remove a tree in Auburn Township?
Generally no. Auburn Township and Geauga County do not require a permit to remove a tree on private residential property. Large-scale clearing may trigger a zoning review, and right-of-way or tree-lawn trees are handled with the township separately. Roubic confirms the requirement for your specific address as part of the free estimate.
How quickly can Roubic remove a tree in Auburn Township?
Standard removals in Auburn Township schedule within 1–3 business days of estimate sign-off. Auburn Township is Roubic's HQ city — crews dispatch straight from the Taylor May Rd yard (0 miles), so active emergencies like a tree on a structure or a blocked driveway get priority response. Call {{global.phone}} for emergency dispatch.
Will Roubic remove an EAB-killed ash tree in Auburn Township?
Yes. Emerald Ash Borer has killed an estimated 90%+ of ash trees across NE Ohio, including Auburn Township. EAB-killed ash turn brittle within 18–24 months and fail violently in storms. We've removed hundreds across the area; sound wood can be chip-dropped to your woodlot or credited as seasoned firewood against the job.
What if the tree is near a house, fence, or power line?
Tight-access removals are routine for our crews. We use sectional dismantling with rigging when bucket-truck access is limited, crane support for heritage trees near structures, and direct coordination with FirstEnergy / The Illuminating Company when work intersects power lines. Insurance documentation is built into every job involving property-protection scenarios.
Can Roubic handle crane-assisted removal of a large heritage tree?
Yes. For 80+ ft heritage trees or removals over structures where standard rigging isn't feasible, Roubic brings owned crane support and ANSI-trained climbers — as we did on an 80 ft white oak that split 6 ft from a roofline. Crane-assisted removals start around $3,500; exact scope and price are confirmed during the free on-site estimate walk.
